summary: Interrogated the project-hierarchy spec against the code it claims to change. One claim was false and was corrected in the draft before this grill was recorded. Three gaps are real and are answered inside the spec's own boundaries; two are sequencing constraints that belong to the plans, not the spec, and are parked.
gaps: The spec claimed the brief 'keeps every heading it already uses' and that the template therefore takes 'an insertion rather than a rewrite'. That is false: docs/product/BRIEF.md uses Summary/Users/Key Flows/Out of Scope while harness/nestjs-react/BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md scaffolds What/Who/Flows/Out of Scope (v1). The two already disagree, so something must be renamed.

The spec requires every story to name a known epic, but plans/roadmap.json on this line has no epics and there is no command that creates one outside the roadmap import ceremony, which needs an accepted epics-approved decision and a digest-bound grill. Enforcing the rule before the command exists would lock this repo out of its own roadmap.
The spec requires every story to reference a confirmed spec, which would delete the roadmap add --no-spec escape hatch that decision 0014 deliberately provides.

The spec says the board reads the hierarchy back, but the board renders no label for the epic or task level at all: EPIC appears zero times in factory/board/index.html and only the drawer says STORY. Projecting more data would not make the levels legible.
The spec's example expectations assume the Riverside example, which lives on feature/realistic-example-project and is not on this line.
resolutions: The brief paragraph was rewritten to state the divergence and name the live brief's set as canonical, with the template realigned onto it; nothing any project has already written is renamed.
The spec introduces forge roadmap epic add as the post-sign-off route that makes the epic requirement satisfiable, and scopes the at-least-one-epic requirement to derive and import.
The spec's Behaviour section states the carve-out explicitly: a story links a confirmed spec OR carries the ad-hoc debt marker, and plan save remains the gate where that debt comes due.
Explicit EPIC and STORY labels and a Project > Epic > Story breadcrumb are named in the Behaviour section, so the labelling is part of the capability rather than a rendering detail.
open_items: non-blocking: the presentation story depends on feature/realistic-example-project being merged first. That is a plan-level sequencing constraint, not a change to the capability.
non-blocking: client repos receive the stricter gates only at re-vendoring, so the rollout runs through forge upgrade rather than retroactively.
